CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Lawrence is a 62-year-old male with past medical history of type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux who presents with complaints of shortness of breath for approximately 10 days. Patient reports noticing some swelling, which he attributes to attending house parties and consuming salty foods. He endorses feeling lethargic. Shortness of breath is exertional, occurring with walking up a flight of stairs. Patient reports leg swelling. He notes mild discomfort when lying flat and stiffness upon waking in the morning that takes time to resolve. Patient reports one episode of acute shortness of breath at night approximately one week ago that has not recurred since. Regarding his diabetes, patient reports blood sugars have been stable with good monitoring during the work week, though he admits to inconsistent monitoring on weekends. Acknowledges affinity for chocolate bars. For depression, patient notes it has been a difficult year and a half. He tried outdoor stretches during summer but has not yet pursued medications and is open to suggestions. Regarding reflux, patient is on omeprazole and has been making lifestyle modifications including reducing Red Bull and caffeine intake. Alcohol intake has been difficult during holiday season but improving. Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorsed shortness of breath on review of systems sheet. Denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 1 diabetes
Congestive heart failure
Depression
Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump
Omeprazole 20 milligrams daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient attends house parties. Consumes salty foods. Acknowledges eating chocolate bars regularly. Reduced alcohol intake during holiday season. Works during the week with weekends being busier.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Pulse oximetry good. Neck exam: No jugular venous distension or carotid bruits appreciated. Heart exam: 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated. Lung exam: Crackles bilaterally at the bases. Lower extremity exam: 1+ pitting edema noted.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease.
Labs: Normal white blood cell count. No evidence of infection or pneumonia.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Shortness of breath/Acute heart failure exacerbation: Patient is retaining fluid likely from dietary indiscretion. Started Lasix 40 milligrams daily. Patient instructed to weigh himself daily and call if weight is not going down or if weight increases. Instructed to call or go to emergency room if shortness of breath worsens at rest, as patient may need intravenous diuretics.

2. Type 1 diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c to be ordered in approximately one month to assess need for adjustments. Patient to follow up with endocrinologist. Patient to ensure recent eye exam is completed.

3. Depression: Referral to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications at this time.

4. Reflux: Continue omeprazole 20 milligrams daily.
